newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-GUERIN RECALLS WINNING GOAL AGAINST BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GUERIN RECALLS WINNING GOAL AGAINST BARCELONA.

text.p: Paris St Germain's Vincent Guerin recounts how he scored a winning goal against Barcelona and hopes for a repeat when the two sides meet again in the European Cup Winners' Cup final in Rotterdam on Wednesday.
"I remember it well. It was a high 40-metre ball out of defence. I took it to within about 20 metres of goal," the France midfielder said.

"I think (Barcelona goalkeeper Carlos) Busquets was unsighted by (Ronald) Koeman and (George) Weah was close, dragging a marker his way. They were surprised when I shot, they probably thought I was going to pass to Weah."
The goal gave PSG a 2-1 victory over Barcelona in Paris in March 1995 and took them through to the semifinals of the European Cup 3-2 on aggregate.

PSG have this season strung five consecutive European semifinals together, a record they share only with Real Madrid and Ajax Amsterdam, on their way to defending the Cup Winners' Cup in their second final.
"We just want to win. I'd be quite happy to win 1-0 with a goal by (goalkeeper Bernard) Lama," Guerin added with a grin.
Should PSG beat Barcelona they will become the first club to retain the Cup Winners' Cup.
Guerin said the present PSG side, coached by former central defender Ricardo, is very different from that of two years ago.
"You can't compare them. There were more experienced players in that team. Now we have several promising young players."
Lama agreed. "If we've got this far it's because we're good, even without Weah and (David) Ginola," he said.
"We're certainly stronger than we were a while ago," he added, looking back over a mid-season slump in which PSG saw their French championship hopes disappear.
Guerin said PSG learned a lot from the winter crisis: "The big lesson this season was to have pulled out of the crisis together."
He said that Barcelona had undergone similarly big changes since the days of coach Johan Cruyff.
"Looking at them from the outside, Barcelona seem to play more as individuals now. They had some strong personalities two years ago but they played more as a team," Guerin said.
Asked whether PSG had any special plans for Barcelona danger man Ronaldo, Guerin said: "We have Brazilians in our side who will be a source of ways of countering him."
Lama said he had no greater concern facing Ronaldo than other Barcelona forwards.
"The problem is not only Ronaldo, there are also others like (Hristo) Stoichkov, my problem is the ball," Lama said. "You can't just focus on Ronaldo, we are facing Barcelona."

Lama said he did not think it was better or worse to have had 10 days without a match before the playing the final, as opposed to Barcelona who met Real Madrid in one of the biggest games of the Spanish season at Camp Nou on Saturday.
"We had four matches in 10 days so it's not bad to have 10 days to recover," France's Euro 96 goalkeeper said.
Lama said French teams had done well against Spanish sides over the years. "The national team too," he said. "I hope it stays that way."
